system_boundary:
Use case: infographic-diagram.
Asset type: a high-resolution English academic manuscript figure, approximately 3200 by 1280 pixels, landscape, pure white background. Flat vector-like scientific illustration, crisp navy text and outlines, no gradients, no shadows, no outer title or figure number. Text large enough for a 7-inch printed figure. Reference images 1 and 2 supply the original manuscript's restrained blue/green device-and-server visual vocabulary only; replace their obsolete architecture and labels with the precise content below.
Primary request: merge the original system architecture and threat-model imagery into ONE clear left-to-right three-role diagram. Three wide aligned panels: pale blue client panel on left, pale green protected reporting panel at center, pale blue server panel on right. Each panel has a small outlined icon (client workstation, shield with key, server tower), one bold header, three short lines or compact internal boxes. Give the central protected panel a dashed green boundary, labeled "CPU TEE boundary". Do not surround the client or server with this boundary.
Exact panel headers and content:
LEFT header "Client training". Internal lines "Training data and objectives"; "GPU model and update"; "Outside the reporting boundary".
CENTER header "Protected report agent". Internal two-part contents: "Bind identity, round and nonce"; "Bind model and update digests"; "Sign with attested key".
RIGHT header "Server audit and aggregation". Lines "Verify report and freshness"; "Audit individual updates"; "Apply state and layer gates".
A solid navy arrow from left to center labeled "Update + telemetry". A solid navy arrow from center to right labeled "Bound report + update". Put arrow labels in clear gaps or above arrows, never over panel text. A thin navy return arrow below the panels goes FROM server TO client labeled "Next model and round".
At the top-left, above the client panel, place one modest red adversary icon with label "Pre-signing attacker". THREE red dashed arrows from this adversary end at client-side inputs only, labeled "Inputs", "Objectives", and "Update". All three terminate in the left client panel before the signing agent; none crosses or falsely depicts defeating the protected reporting process.

Prefer icons and clean blocks over dense text. No data plots or numeric performance claims. Ensure all arrowheads and English labels are unambiguous.
five_stage_framework:
Use case: infographic-diagram.
Asset type: a high-resolution English academic manuscript method overview, approximately 3200 by 1500 pixels, pure white background. Flat vector-like scientific diagram with crisp navy text and outlines, restrained pastel color panels, readable large type for a 7-inch printed figure. Use the reference image ONLY for the recognizable five-stage, five-color, snake-flow composition of the original manuscript. Update ALL content as below; do not copy obsolete labels or formulas.
Composition: five rounded rectangular stage cards. Top row: stage 1 blue, stage 2 orange, stage 3 purple, all equally sized. Bottom row: stage 5 green on the left (half width), stage 4 rose on the right (half width). CLEAR solid navy arrowheads connect 1 to 2 to 3, then down from 3 to 4, then left from 4 to 5. A thin feedback arrow follows the outside left perimeter from stage 5 back to stage 1, labeled "Next round". Avoid crossing arrows. Each stage has a compact meaningful outline icon, bold numbered heading, and exactly three generously spaced internal lines labelled INPUT, OPERATION, OUTPUT. Each of those three labels should be small uppercase but contents must be prominent. No global title or figure number.
Exact contents:
Stage 1 heading "1  Admission and runtime evidence"
INPUT: "Signed report + update"
OPERATION: "Verify binding; filter runtime evidence"
OUTPUT: "Valid submission + trust score"
Stage 2 heading "2  Content audit"
INPUT: "Current update + server reference"
OPERATION: "Server audit; optional peer checks"
OUTPUT: "Quality and instantaneous risk"
Stage 3 heading "3  History and state evolution"
INPUT: "Current quality and risk"
OPERATION: "Update history, risk EMA and state"
OUTPUT: "Credibility and participation state"
Stage 4 heading "4  Layer aggregation"
INPUT: "Eligible updates + layer statistics"
OPERATION: "Gate with G; weight with F; clip"
OUTPUT: "Surviving block increments"
Stage 5 heading "5  Global update and feedback"
INPUT: "Surviving block increments"
OPERATION: "Apply increments; broadcast model"
OUTPUT: "Next model and round identifier"
A narrow note strip at the bottom with exact text: "Freeze peer membership before state transitions. Apply eligibility after transitions." Second line: "Recovery evidence uses the server audit; missing peers do not block recovery."
Constraints: keep five distinct pastel panel colors and the recognizable original five-stage flow, but greatly simplify the internals. Do NOT include any standalone state-machine inset: detailed transitions are supplied in a separate manuscript table. No equation-heavy internals, no Secure Aggregation label, no numerical performance claims. No arrow from stage 2 directly to stage 4, no skipped stages. Gate uses G; weights use F.
layer_aggregation:
Use case: infographic-diagram.
Asset type: a high-resolution English academic manuscript algorithm diagram, approximately 3400 by 1700 pixels, pure white background. Flat vector-like academic illustration, crisp navy text and lines, large carefully typeset mathematical symbols. Use the reference image as the layout and palette reference: THREE TALL COLUMNS, pale BLUE evidence inputs on the left, pale ORANGE layer-wise decisions in the middle, pale GREEN constrained execution on the right. Retain that familiar three-column structure but replace every old formula and label with the content below. No external title or figure number. Generous whitespace and readable math at 7-inch print width.
Top headers: "Evidence inputs", "Layer-wise decision", "Constrained execution".
LEFT column, three stacked internal cards connected by down arrows:
1. "Eligible client updates" with "After state transitions" and "NORMAL / SUSPECT".
2. "Two distinct scores" with two prominent separate formulas in correct mathematical typesetting: "Raw credibility: F_k" and "Gate score: G_k = F_k / U_{n_k^e}". Render all subscripts/superscripts properly. Caption "Evidence-age envelope U".
3. "Layer evidence" with "Heuristic depth prior"; "Server-reference utility"; "Eligible-peer disagreement". Do NOT say privacy sensitivity or privacy guarantee.
MIDDLE column, three stacked internal cards connected by down arrows:
1. "Sensitivity" with the large mathematical label "S_l" and short line "Depth + utility + disagreement".
2. "Bounded gate" with the EXACT formula, typeset cleanly as a fraction: theta_l = 0.4 + 0.6 * (1.2 S_l)/(1 + 1.2 S_l). Use Greek theta, subscript l, mathematical multiplication by adjacency, not code. Do not omit 0.6 or either 1.2.
3. "Block clipping radius" with the EXACT formula C_l = C_{base,l}/(1 + S_l). Beneath it short two-line note "C_base: median block norm" and "No eligible peers: server block norm". The base index is base,l, not just base. Radius applies to each parameter block, not the full update.
RIGHT column, three stacked internal cards connected by down arrows:
1. "Survivors: Phi_l" (Greek capital Phi with subscript l), prominent condition "G_k >= theta_l" properly typeset with greater-than-or-equal symbol and Greek theta. Supporting line "Eligible, F_k > 0, nonzero block".
2. "Normalize with raw credibility" with the EXACT typeset fraction formula w_k^(l) = (n_k F_k) / (sum over j in Phi_l of n_j F_j). Use true mathematical superscripts/subscripts, capital Phi. Gate score G must NOT appear in this weight formula.
3. "Clip and aggregate" with short lines "Clip each survivor at C_l" and "Sum weighted block increments".
Horizontal arrows LEFT to MIDDLE and MIDDLE to RIGHT only in clear gutters. A footer strip across the entire figure has two strong concise rules: "Gate with G; weight with F." and "Empty survivor set or zero radius: no block update."
Constraints: all formulas and dependencies must match exactly. Retain blue/orange/green three-panel layout. No fallback to quarantined clients, no secure aggregation, no privacy guarantee, no data curves or numerical outcome claims. Draw polished readable scientific math, never tiny formula text.
